steps.name: TF activity with decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI
caveats: A prior network is tissue-agnostic: a kidney-specific regulator with few curated edges can be missed, and targets silent in kidney add noise. Say so rather than treating rank order as biology

With 6 per group the limma per-regulator test is modestly powered; a non-significant TF is not evidence of no regulation
steps.context: Twelve samples total; the design is 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle-control human kidney. A regulatory network inferred from this expression matrix alone would be noise (mutual-information regulon inference needs roughly 100+ samples), and VIPER/ARACNe are not installed here, so a prior-knowledge network with a linear-model estimator is the only sound route. Aldosterone signals through the mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2) and cross-reacts with NR3C1; whether those regulators surface is a coherence check on the inference, not a target of a filter — do not restrict the regulon set to expected TFs.
steps.question: Which transcription factors show altered inferred activity in aldosterone-treated kidney samples relative to vehicle controls?

constraints: Use the univariate linear model (ulm) estimator; mlm may be reported as a secondary estimator but ulm is primary

steps.description: This is the answer step. Needs a curated, signed human TF-target regulon network — resolve it from the reference store (a human TF-target regulon table with source, target, and a signed mode-of-regulation weight; CollecTRI human is the preferred collection and was present in the store at planning time). Run two complementary decoupleR univariate linear model (ulm) inferences and report both. (a) Contrast-level: run ulm on the unshrunken Wald statistic of EVERY gene tested in T1S2 — not the significant subset — to get one activity score and p-value per TF for the aldosterone vs vehicle contrast. (b) Per-sample: run ulm on a log2 CPM matrix built from the filtered counts (one column per sample), giving a score per TF per sample, then test aldosterone vs vehicle on the score matrix with limma under the same ~condition design and adjust across regulators with Benjamini-Hochberg. Keep only regulators with at least 5 targets among the tested genes and report how many regulators entered each test. Preserve the sign of each edge so a repressed target lowers rather than raises a score. Output: the ranked contrast-level TF table, the per-sample score matrix, the limma per-regulator test table, a heatmap of the per-sample scores for the top regulators by absolute score, and a barplot of the top up and down TFs with the direction defined as positive = higher activity in aldosterone-treated. acceptance_criteria: Regulon network resolved from the reference store, with its name, version, number of TFs and number of edges reported; human confirmed

Top up- and down-activity TFs listed with explicit direction (positive = higher in aldosterone-treated), and their scores from the contrast-level and per-sample routes shown side by side
Report states explicitly that an activity score is an inference from a curated prior network, not a measurement

steps.question: Do the top transcription factors called for aldosterone vs vehicle survive a change of prior regulon network?

constraints: Keep the confidence filter to levels A through C and state it; do not include D or E
Use the same Wald statistic input and the same ulm estimator as T2S1 — the only variable changed is the network

Contrast-level ulm rerun with identical input statistic, estimator, and minimum regulon size
A comparison table naming TFs significant in both networks, and TFs significant in only one, with the network identified

steps.name: PROGENy pathway footprints as upstream context

steps.question: Which signalling pathway footprints accompany the transcription factor activity changes in aldosterone-treated versus vehicle kidney samples?

grounding.reason: Pathway activity with the PROGENy footprint model via decoupleR mlm on the contrast statistic, top 500 responsive genes, read as footprint not membership (R-0115); SPIA topology is absent from this environment (R-0122)

constraints: Use the mlm estimator with the top 500 responsive genes per pathway
Run on the full ranked Wald statistic, not on a thresholded gene set
Do not claim pathway topology or directional signal flow — the footprint model has none
steps.description: Run decoupleR multivariate linear model (mlm) with a human signalling-pathway footprint model (PROGENy; resolve the weighted perturbation-response gene sets from the reference store or the installed decoupleR/OmniPath resources, using the top 500 responsive genes per pathway) on the T1S2 Wald statistic across all tested genes, giving one pathway activity score and p-value per pathway for the aldosterone vs vehicle contrast. Also compute per-sample pathway scores on the log2 CPM matrix so the spread across the 6+6 samples is visible. Report scores as transcriptional footprints, explicitly not as expression of pathway member genes. Place the result beside the TF table: a pathway footprint that is upstream of a top-scoring TF is supporting context for it. If the footprint model cannot be resolved at run time, report its absence — the TF answer in T2S1/T2S2 stands without it.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway footprint model resolved with its name and version reported, or its absence reported plainly
Contrast-level mlm pathway activity table produced with score and adjusted p-value per pathway
Per-sample pathway score matrix and heatmap produced across the 12 samples

steps.name: Integrated TF report and reproducibility record
caveats: The whole inference rests on curated human regulons that are not kidney-specific; the report must not present rank order as biological certainty
Six samples per group gives wide uncertainty on every per-regulator test
steps.context: The synthesizer reads this report. Without the explicit network-and-estimator provenance and the inference caution, a ranked TF table reads as a measured result, which it is not.
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to which transcription factors drive the aldosterone response, and with what stated uncertainty?

grounding.reason: Activity report fields (network, version, statistic, contrast, estimator, min regulon size, regulator count, inference caution) per R-0119, plus the reproducibility record per R-0086

constraints: Direction must be stated as positive = higher activity in aldosterone-treated relative to vehicle control, matching the T1S2 contrast
Do not promote a TF to a conclusion on the strength of one network and one route
Do not report a mechanistic claim about aldosterone signalling that the tables do not support
steps.description: Assemble the outputs of T1S1, T1S2, T2S1, T2S2, and T2S3 into one report. Lead with the ranked transcription factors for the aldosterone vs vehicle contrast, giving for each: activity score and adjusted p-value from the contrast-level inference, the per-sample limma test result, whether the second regulon network agreed, the number of its targets among the tested genes, and its own transcript's differential expression from T1S2. Separate the TFs supported by both networks and both inference routes from those supported by one only. State for every activity result: the network name and version, the input statistic (DESeq2 Wald, contrast aldosterone vs vehicle), the estimator (ulm), the minimum regulon size (5), the number of regulators tested, and the caution that an activity score is an inference from a prior network and not a measurement — a top-ranked TF is a hypothesis for experimental follow-up. acceptance_criteria: A single ranked TF table combining contrast-level score, per-sample limma result, cross-network agreement, target count, and the TF's own differential expression
TFs concordant across both networks and both inference routes reported separately from single-source calls
Network name and version, input statistic, contrast direction, estimator, minimum regulon size, and number of regulators tested all stated
Explicit statement that activity scores are network-based inferences and top TFs are hypotheses for follow-up
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed, and every collection version consumed

plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: TF activity inference
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks which transcription factors drive the aldosterone-treated kidney samples relative to vehicle controls, from a 12,000 gene x 12 sample raw Salmon count matrix (counts.csv) with a one-column metadata table (metadata.csv, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle control, unpaired, single batch). Twelve samples is far too few to infer a regulatory network from the expression itself (a mutual-information regulon needs ~100 samples), so every TF statement here comes from a prior-knowledge signed regulon network — CollecTRI human, which is present in the reference store, with DoRothEA human (confidence A-C) also present as the robustness network. VIPER/ARACNe, the tools of record for a context-specific regulon, are not installed; decoupleR is (v2.2.0), so the linear-model estimators substitute for them and the report must say so.

The flow is: (T1S1) sample-structure QC on blind-VST values — PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes — to confirm the two condition groups separate and no sample is an outlier before anything is fitted; (T1S2) the gene-level contrast itself, DESeq2 Wald aldosterone vs vehicle with control set explicitly as the reference level, minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), apeglm shrinkage for reporting/ranking, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering left on and the p-value histogram inspected. The unshrunken Wald statistic from this step is the input the TF inference needs — it scales each gene's effect by its uncertainty, which a raw fold change does not. (T2S1) is the answer step: decoupleR ulm run two ways on the CollecTRI regulons — once on the Wald statistic of every tested gene to give one activity score per TF for the contrast, and once per sample on log2 CPM so the scores can be tested between groups with limma and BH across regulators. Both are kept because a contrast score without the per-sample spread hides whether one sample carries the signal. Minimum regulon size 5, edge signs kept so a repressed target lowers rather than raises the score. (T2S2) repeats the inference on DoRothEA A-C and reports the overlap and disagreement of the top regulators, since a single prior network is one opinion. (T2S3) adds PROGENy pathway-activity footprints via decoupleR mlm as upstream context for whichever TFs come out — aldosterone acts through NR3C2/NR3C1, so a mineralocorticoid-consistent footprint is a coherence check, not an independent result. (T1S3) writes the report: network name and version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, minimum regulon size, number of regulators tested, and the explicit caution that an activity score is an inference from a curated network and not a measurement — a top-ranked TF is a hypothesis for follow-up.

Two limits stated up front. The counts are Salmon-derived and already summarised to gene symbols in a single CSV; transcript-level abundances and average transcript lengths are not in the inputs, so no length offset can be carried into the model and no isoform-level question can be answered. And six per group supports the contrast but leaves the per-regulator limma test modestly powered, so absence of a significant TF is not evidence of no regulation.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Pre-filter: at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
DESeq2 design ~condition with control as reference level
DESeq2 Wald test, aldosterone vs vehicle
apeglm shrinkage of the condition coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg with DESeq2 independent filtering, p-value histogram diagnostic
decoupleR ulm on the CollecTRI regulons, per-sample log2 CPM scores plus ulm on the Wald statistic of the contrast
decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy footprint model
Activity report with network version, statistic, estimator, regulator count, inference caution, plus reproducibility record

acceptance_criteria: Regulon network resolved from the reference store, with its name, version, number of TFs and number of edges reported; human confirmed
Contrast-level ulm run on the Wald statistic of all tested genes, producing a ranked TF activity table with score and BH-adjusted p-value
Per-sample ulm score matrix produced on log2 CPM, and a limma ~condition test on those scores with BH across regulators
Number of regulators passing the min-5-target filter stated for each inference
Top up- and down-activity TFs listed with explicit direction (positive = higher in aldosterone-treated), and their scores from the contrast-level and per-sample routes shown side by side
Report states explicitly that an activity score is an inference from a curated prior network, not a measurement
constraints: Use the univariate linear model (ulm) estimator; mlm may be reported as a secondary estimator but ulm is primary
Feed the contrast inference the full ranked list of tested genes — never a padj- or fold-change-thresholded subset
Set minimum regulon size to 5 targets present among the tested genes
Keep the signed mode-of-regulation weight on every edge; do not binarize or take absolute values
Do not infer a regulatory network from this expression matrix — 12 samples cannot support it; state this in the output
Do not filter the regulon set to a hypothesis-driven shortlist of TFs before the test
Gene identifiers in the counts are HGNC symbols; match them to the regulon symbol space and report the share of tested genes that matched
caveats: A prior network is tissue-agnostic: a kidney-specific regulator with few curated edges can be missed, and targets silent in kidney add noise. Say so rather than treating rank order as biology

A high-scoring TF whose own transcript does not change is still plausible — activity is footprint-based — but so is a spurious hit; check the TF's own expression in the T1S2 table and report it beside the score
With 6 per group the limma per-regulator test is modestly powered; a non-significant TF is not evidence of no regulation

grounding.reason: TF activity is the research question: decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI, both on the contrast Wald statistic (R-0111) and per-sample with limma on the scores and BH across regulators (R-0112); prior network only because 12 samples cannot support network inference (R-0121) and VIPER/ARACNe are absent (R-0114)

steps.name: Regulon robustness on DoRothEA A-C
steps.question: Do the top transcription factors called for aldosterone vs vehicle survive a change of prior regulon network?
steps.description: Repeat the contrast-level decoupleR ulm inference from T2S1 on a second human TF regulon resource — a confidence-graded signed regulon set filtered to its high-confidence levels (DoRothEA human, confidence A to C, was present in the reference store at planning time; it is an R serialized data frame with tf/confidence/target/mor columns to be renamed to source/target/weight). Same input statistic (the T1S2 Wald statistic for all tested genes), same estimator, same minimum regulon size of 5. Report the overlap and the disagreement between the two networks' top regulators: the rank correlation of scores over TFs present in both, the TFs called significant by both, and the TFs called by only one, naming which. Treat concordant calls as the defensible answer and single-network calls as weaker. If the second network is absent at run time, report that only one network was available and that no cross-network robustness statement can be made — this does not invalidate T2S1.
steps.context: CollecTRI and DoRothEA differ in coverage and curation, and a TF that appears only in one is a network artefact as often as a finding. This step costs little and is what separates a reportable regulator from a ranked row.
acceptance_criteria: Second regulon network resolved, filtered to its high-confidence levels, with the levels kept and the number of TFs and edges stated
Contrast-level ulm rerun with identical input statistic, estimator, and minimum regulon size
A comparison table naming TFs significant in both networks, and TFs significant in only one, with the network identified
Rank correlation of TF scores across the two networks reported
If the second network is absent, that fact reported plainly with no substitute network silently used
constraints: Keep the confidence filter to levels A through C and state it; do not include D or E
Use the same Wald statistic input and the same ulm estimator as T2S1 — the only variable changed is the network
Keep the signed mor weight; rename tf/target/mor to source/target/weight for the decoupleR network argument
caveats: The two networks overlap substantially in their best-supported edges, so agreement is partly structural and is not independent replication
DoRothEA levels A-C still mix curated and ChIP-derived evidence; a concordant call is more credible than a single-network call but is not validation

grounding.reason: DoRothEA confidence A-C is the named alternative regulon set (R-0113), and the report must give the overlap and disagreement of the top regulators when two networks run (R-0119)

steps.name: PROGENy pathway footprints as upstream context
steps.question: Which signalling pathway footprints accompany the transcription factor activity changes in aldosterone-treated versus vehicle kidney samples?
steps.description: Run decoupleR multivariate linear model (mlm) with a human signalling-pathway footprint model (PROGENy; resolve the weighted perturbation-response gene sets from the reference store or the installed decoupleR/OmniPath resources, using the top 500 responsive genes per pathway) on the T1S2 Wald statistic across all tested genes, giving one pathway activity score and p-value per pathway for the aldosterone vs vehicle contrast. Also compute per-sample pathway scores on the log2 CPM matrix so the spread across the 6+6 samples is visible. Report scores as transcriptional footprints, explicitly not as expression of pathway member genes. Place the result beside the TF table: a pathway footprint that is upstream of a top-scoring TF is supporting context for it. If the footprint model cannot be resolved at run time, report its absence — the TF answer in T2S1/T2S2 stands without it.
steps.context: Aldosterone acts through a nuclear receptor, so pathway footprints are secondary context rather than the answer. This step is included because the recommended procedure pairs it with the TF inference and because it constrains over-interpretation of a lone TF hit.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway footprint model resolved with its name and version reported, or its absence reported plainly
Contrast-level mlm pathway activity table produced with score and adjusted p-value per pathway
Per-sample pathway score matrix and heatmap produced across the 12 samples
Output states in words that a footprint score is not the expression of pathway member genes and carries no pathway topology
constraints: Use the mlm estimator with the top 500 responsive genes per pathway
Run on the full ranked Wald statistic, not on a thresholded gene set
Do not claim pathway topology or directional signal flow — the footprint model has none
caveats: PROGENy covers a small set of canonical signalling pathways and contains no mineralocorticoid receptor pathway; a null result here says nothing about aldosterone signalling
Pathway and TF footprints are estimated from the same gene statistics, so agreement between them is not independent evidence

grounding.reason: Pathway activity with the PROGENy footprint model via decoupleR mlm on the contrast statistic, top 500 responsive genes, read as footprint not membership (R-0115); SPIA topology is absent from this environment (R-0122)

steps.name: Integrated TF report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to which transcription factors drive the aldosterone response, and with what stated uncertainty?
steps.description: Assemble the outputs of T1S1, T1S2, T2S1, T2S2, and T2S3 into one report. Lead with the ranked transcription factors for the aldosterone vs vehicle contrast, giving for each: activity score and adjusted p-value from the contrast-level inference, the per-sample limma test result, whether the second regulon network agreed, the number of its targets among the tested genes, and its own transcript's differential expression from T1S2. Separate the TFs supported by both networks and both inference routes from those supported by one only. State for every activity result: the network name and version, the input statistic (DESeq2 Wald, contrast aldosterone vs vehicle), the estimator (ulm), the minimum regulon size (5), the number of regulators tested, and the caution that an activity score is an inference from a prior network and not a measurement — a top-ranked TF is a hypothesis for experimental follow-up. Record the limitations plainly: 6 per group, no transcript-length offset available from the provided gene-level matrix, tissue-agnostic prior network, and that a non-significant regulator is not evidence of no regulation. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, any random seed used, and the version of every regulon and pathway collection consumed.
steps.context: The synthesizer reads this report. Without the explicit network-and-estimator provenance and the inference caution, a ranked TF table reads as a measured result, which it is not.
acceptance_criteria: A single ranked TF table combining contrast-level score, per-sample limma result, cross-network agreement, target count, and the TF's own differential expression
TFs concordant across both networks and both inference routes reported separately from single-source calls
Network name and version, input statistic, contrast direction, estimator, minimum regulon size, and number of regulators tested all stated
Explicit statement that activity scores are network-based inferences and top TFs are hypotheses for follow-up
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seed, and every collection version consumed
constraints: Direction must be stated as positive = higher activity in aldosterone-treated relative to vehicle control, matching the T1S2 contrast
Do not promote a TF to a conclusion on the strength of one network and one route
Do not report a mechanistic claim about aldosterone signalling that the tables do not support
caveats: The whole inference rests on curated human regulons that are not kidney-specific; the report must not present rank order as biological certainty
Six samples per group gives wide uncertainty on every per-regulator test

grounding.reason: Activity report fields (network, version, statistic, contrast, estimator, min regulon size, regulator count, inference caution) per R-0119, plus the reproducibility record per R-0086
